title: Accounting foundations
goal: Explain where any transaction goes: which company, which account, debit or credit, and which report it shows up on.
concept_card: Every transaction answers four questions: which company, which account, which property or job, and what document proves it. Debits raise assets and expenses; credits raise liabilities, equity and income. Each company keeps its own books.
lesson_html:
The accounting equation. Everything in the books follows one rule: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Assets are what a company owns (cash, houses held for sale, equipment). Liabilities are what it owes (loans, unpaid bills). Equity is what is left for the owner.

Debits and credits. Every entry has at least one debit and one credit, and they are always equal.

Account typeGoes up withExamples
AssetDebitChecking account, property held for sale, tools
ExpenseDebitOffice rent, fuel, software
LiabilityCreditAccounts payable, hard-money loan, credit card
EquityCreditOwner's investment, retained earnings
IncomeCreditSale of a house, plumbing service revenue

Cash basis vs accrual basis. Cash basis records income and costs when money moves. Accrual basis records them when they are earned or incurred, even if not yet paid. A plumber finishes work on September 28 and invoices you October 5: on accrual basis that cost belongs to September.

The three main reports.

  • Balance Sheet: what the company owns and owes on one day.
  • Profit and Loss (P&L): income minus expenses over a period, such as September.
  • Statement of Cash Flows: where cash came from and where it went.

Four companies, four sets of books. Twin Home Buyer / Equity Track, Matrix Group One, Peninsula Plumbing Solutions and Equity Track PH are separate legal entities. When one pays a bill that belongs to another, you record money owed between them (intercompany). You never just book the expense in whichever company paid.
rule: Every transaction answers four questions: Which company? Which account? Which property or job? What document proves it?

qbo_steps.title: Switch between companies
qbo_steps.html: Gear icon ⚙ → Switch company. Check the company name at the top left before you enter anything.

qbo_steps.title: Open the chart of accounts
qbo_steps.html: ⚙ → Chart of accounts. Look at each account's type and detail type. Print or export it; you'll build a cheat sheet from it.

qbo_steps.title: Run the Balance Sheet and P&L
qbo_steps.html: Reports → Balance Sheet and Reports → Profit and Loss. Set the dates to last month.

qbo_steps.title: Check the accounting basis
qbo_steps.html: On any report, look for the Cash / Accrual setting and note which one the CPA wants.

qbo_steps.title: Trace one transaction
qbo_steps.html: Click any number on the P&L to drill down to the transaction, then open the original bill or receipt attached to it.

scenario.text_html: Equity Track PH has $512,000 in assets: $38,000 cash and one house held for sale at $474,000. It owes $331,500 on a hard-money loan and $1,500 in unpaid bills.
scenario.followup: Peninsula Plumbing finishes a job on the 30th and invoices on the 2nd. Which month is the revenue in on accrual basis?

quiz.q: Twin Home Buyer buys $2,000 of tools with cash. What is the entry?
options: Debit Tools expense, credit Accounts payable
No entry until the tools are used
quiz.why: Tools go up (asset, debit). Cash goes down (asset, credit). Ask the CPA about the threshold for recording tools as an asset or an expense.
quiz.followup: Twin Home Buyer pays a $600 insurance premium for 12 months up front. What gets debited on day one?

quiz.q: A customer pays Peninsula Plumbing $2,000 for a job. What is the entry?
options: No entry until the end of the month
quiz.why: Money came into the bank, and the bank is an asset, so it goes up with a debit. The company earned the money, and income goes up with a credit.

quiz.q: On accrual basis, when do you record a contractor's cost?
quiz.why: Accrual basis records the cost in the period the work happened, even if the bill is paid later.

quiz.q: Matrix Group One pays a $3,000 invoice that belongs to Twin Home Buyer. How is it recorded?
options: Expense in Twin Home Buyer only, nothing in Matrix
Matrix records money owed by Twin Home Buyer; Twin Home Buyer records the expense and money owed to Matrix
Ignore it; the same owner owns both
quiz.why: Both companies record it: a due-from in Matrix and the expense plus a due-to in Twin Home Buyer. The two balances must match.

options: Income and expenses for a month
What the company owns and owes on one date
quiz.why: The Balance Sheet is a snapshot on one date. The P&L covers a period.

task: Take 10 real transactions from last month for one company. For each, write the company, account, property/job, debit/credit and the document that proves it. Your reviewer checks them.
rubric: At least 9 of 10 coded to the right company and account
Every line names its source document
Debits equal credits on every entry
Explains any item she wasn't sure about
